lead.headline: WAYMO EXPANDS DRIVERLESS FLEET TO FOUR MORE US CITIES
lead.summary: The driverless revolution is moving at a breakneck pace as Waymo expands its fully autonomous taxi service to four more American cities. The fleet currently handles a staggering half a million paid rides every single week, with eyes set on hitting the million mark before the year's end. Investors are cheering the rapid tenfold growth over just two years, signaling a major shift in public transit.

stories.headline: Tesla Begins Cybercab Tests For Employees in Texas
stories.summary: Elon Musk’s outfit is taking its first tentative steps toward a pedal-less future by launching employee rides in the new 'Cybercab' at Giga Texas. The catch is that these driverless tests are strictly confined to a parking lot for now. Millions of eager onlookers watched the announcement online, waiting to see if the wheel-less wonder can handle the real open road.

stories.headline: NHTSA Orders Robotaxi Operators to Fix Safety Flaws
stories.summary: Federal watchdogs are putting the brakes on autonomous vehicle operators, demanding that industry leaders Waymo and Tesla fix dangerous bugs in their software. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration warns that with more driverless cars hitting the pavement, the kinks must be ironed out immediately. The move comes after several close calls and traffic incidents raised eyebrows in Washington.

stories.headline: New Jersey Proposes Ban on Lidar-Less Self-Driving Cars
stories.summary: The Garden State is drawing a line in the sand with a new bill that could outlaw autonomous vehicles operating without radar and lidar sensors. The legislative threat directly targets Tesla's vision-only approach, even as the company gains ground in China. If passed, the law could spark a major tech showdown on New Jersey turnpikes.

stories.headline: Waymo In-Cabin Cameras Spark Police Investigation
stories.summary: Big Brother is riding shotgun in the driverless age, as police in San Mateo recently searched a Waymo robotaxi after the company reported underage passengers on board. The incident highlights the constant surveillance inside the cabs, which are equipped with active microphones and cameras. Remote agents keep a watchful eye on rowdy riders, reminding passengers that they are never truly alone.

stories.headline: Robotic Pods Proposed to Clean and Charge Robotaxis
stories.summary: Aseon Labs is planning to dot municipal landscapes with automated maintenance pods designed to clean, inspect, and juice up robotaxis on the fly. These robotic pit stops aim to keep driverless fleets running smoothly closer to their passengers. However, city planners are already sweating over where to put these mechanical hubs.

lead.headline: APPLE SUES OPENAI IN EXPLOSIVE TRADE SECRETS CLASH
lead.summary: The tech world has been rocked by a blockbuster lawsuit as Apple drags OpenAI into court, accusing the startup of orchestrating a brazen raid on its top engineering talent. The legal battle centers on a damning leak where a former Apple engineer sent a cheeky 'LOL' message boasting about accessing proprietary trade secrets. The clash marks a fierce escalation in the high-stakes battle for artificial intelligence supremacy.

stories.headline: Protesters March on Silicon Valley Giants Demanding AI Halt
stories.summary: A roaring crowd of two hundred demonstrators took to the streets of San Francisco, marching on the headquarters of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind. The angry picketers demanded an immediate halt to the corporate AI arms race, voicing deep fears over the technology's rapid rise. The protest brought the anxieties of the machine age directly to the doorsteps of its creators.

stories.headline: Uncle Sam Moves to Restrict Chinese Open-Weight Models
stories.summary: The federal government is tightening the screws on foreign tech, moving to place strict limits on open-weight AI models coming out of China. Officials in Washington are sounding the alarm over distillation risks, fearing these models could bypass domestic security. Analysts warn the crackdown might inadvertently fuel a boom in decentralized, off-grid crypto AI projects.

stories.headline: Zuckerberg Admits Meta AI Bets Yet to Bear Fruit
stories.summary: Meta chieftain Mark Zuckerberg threw a bucket of cold water on Wall Street, admitting that the company's massive artificial intelligence gambit has not yet paid off. The sobering confession sent Meta shares tumbling five percent in trading. Despite the lack of immediate returns, the social media giant is still projected to pour up to $145 billion into the AI gold rush this year.

stories.headline: Tech Giant TCS to Mobilize Army of AI Engineers
stories.summary: India's premier IT outfit, Tata Consultancy Services, is gearing up for a massive recruitment drive to build a force of up to 8,900 AI deployment engineers. The firm is also hunting for strategic acquisitions to protect its business from automated disruptions. TCS is betting big that the AI revolution will generate fresh contracts rather than kill the tech services industry.

stories.headline: Banking Giant Warns AI Amplifies Global Cybersecurity Risks
stories.summary: Wall Street titan Jamie Dimon has issued a stark warning, declaring that artificial intelligence is supercharging the threat of global cyber warfare. Citing powerful systems like Anthropic's tech, the JPMorgan Chase chief cautioned that bad actors could weaponize the tools. The warning underscores an urgent need for financial institutions to shore up their digital defenses.

stories.headline: Machine Bots Now Outnumber Humans on World Wide Web
stories.summary: The internet is fast becoming a ghost town for actual humans, as new reports reveal that automated bots now make up the vast majority of web traffic. These digital crawlers and automated agents are dominating the wires, leaving real flesh-and-blood users in the minority. Critics warn we are now living in an AI-dominated web where humans are merely rats in the digital walls.
